core.title: Declare named themes on every user/system flow; keep them out of the user/system flow id
core.given: A user/system flow exists in, or is being added to, the plan.
core.when: The planner authors, edits or reviews that user/system flow.
core.then: Declare one or more named themes on the user/system flow, drawn from the repository-defined theme taxonomy.
prefer: Treat themes as named plan metadata that classifies the journey the user/system flow covers.
Keep the user/system flow identity in the typed user/system flow URN shape defined by the stack.
Take theme values from the taxonomy as defined: it reserves zero as commons (reserved_zero = commons) and other values are repository-defined; do not infer further semantics for the reserved value.
avoid: Encoding a theme in the user/system flow identity (e.g. a theme number or theme prefix in the id); digits that do not encode a theme are not affected.
Reviving a retired numeric theme-range scheme to derive or reserve user/system flow ids.
Leaving a user/system flow with no declared theme.
core.why: Themes classify the journey, while identity is the typed user/system flow URN; keeping them separate means classification is metadata and is never encoded in identity.
evidence: Every user/system flow in the plan declares one or more named themes (in whatever representation the plan uses).
Declared themes are values of the repository-defined theme taxonomy.
User/system flow ids match the typed user/system flow URN shape and contain no theme encoding.
verification: A plan-level check covers every user/system flow: each must declare one or more named themes that are values of the repository-defined theme taxonomy (themes are repository-defined plan metadata); where the taxonomy lives is profile data.
Validate the user/system flow id against the typed user/system flow URN shape independently of the theme check; only theme-encoding in the id is a finding, not the mere presence of digits.

Theme values are taken exactly as the taxonomy defines them: the taxonomy reserves zero as commons (reserved_zero = commons) and its other values are repository-defined; the check infers no further semantics for the reserved zero.

Activation by plan-artifact location is a hint, not a gate: a user/system flow defined in any artifact, inside or outside the plan tree, is in scope, and the check applies regardless of which user/system flow field was touched.

values: user/system flow defined or modified (any field)
user/system flow id encodes a theme

fires: The planner creates a new user/system flow.
The planner edits any part of an existing user/system flow (themes, id, its list of work items, description or other metadata).
The planner reviews or validates the plan and its user/system flows.
A user/system flow definition appears in any artifact, inside or outside the plan tree.
doesNotFire: Work that neither defines, edits nor reviews any user/system flow (e.g. code changes containing no user/system flow definition).

profileRequirements.meaning: The typed identity shape of a user/system flow; the core requires every user/system flow id to match it and to carry no theme encoding.
Where plan artifacts (including user/system flow definitions) live; the core uses this only as an activation hint, never as a scope gate.
The file that declares the repository-defined theme taxonomy from which user/system flow themes must be drawn (proposed key).

bunOnly.reason: The term id and label belong to this rule's realization registry; every other part of this verifier detail is stack-independent and lives in the core verification (taxonomy membership, the zero-as-commons reservation, no inferred semantics) or is realized through the taxonomy-source profile key.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is fully neutral: declare named themes drawn from the repository-defined taxonomy and keep them out of the typed train identity, including the taxonomy's zero-as-commons reservation and the prohibition on inferring further semantics for it — that reservation is stack-independent domain policy and is preserved verbatim in the core (prefer and verification), not deferred to the realization. Three things could not be made neutral and stay with the profile or the realization: (1) the concrete identity shape train:{subject}:{slug}, delivered as the urn.train profile value; (2) the taxonomy source path plan/_themes.yaml, delivered via the proposed layout.registries#theme_taxonomy profile key; (3) this rule's term id and label (theme_taxonomy / 'Themes'), which belong to the realization registry and are recorded in bunOnly. The retired numeric theme-range scheme is kept verbatim in avoid because it names no stack; for stacks without that legacy it is vacuous, adding no obligation. The Bun phrase 'wagons list' was generalized to 'its list of work items' in fires, with the concrete term preserved in bun.json as the reference example.
